## Circular to SFC's Registered Intermediaries

## Order Recording Requirements

An  intermediary  is  expected  under  paragraph  3.9  of  the  Code  of  Conduct  for  Persons Registered with the SFC (the 'Code') to use a telephone recording system to record order instructions of a client if he receives the instructions from the client through the telephone. The telephone recordings should be retained by the intermediary as part of its records for at least three months.

These requirements have become effective for over a year since 1 October 2001. We note with  concern  that  certain  registered  intermediaries  are  not  yet  complying  fully  with  the requirements laid down in the Code. We have identified, in our on-site examination of the intermediaries, the following common types of shortcomings:

- (1) Failure to connect all telephone lines on which your staff is permitted to receive order instructions from a client to a tape recording system;
- (2) Failure to adopt any effective order recording procedures to maintain a reliable record of  the  time  of  receipt  and  order  details  where  order  instructions  are  received  by mobile phones;
- (3) Failure to establish effective procedures to ensure the integrity, reliability and security of the tape recording system and the timely detection of any malfunctioning;
- (4) Failure to exercise adequate  compliance  monitoring  over your staff  who  are responsible for recording the telephone order instructions; and
- (5) Failure to retain the telephone recordings for a minimum period of three months.

Telephone  recordings of client orders is an integral part of the audit trails  which intermediaries should maintain in order to facilitate the resolution of any trade disputes. In addition, it is an effective compliance monitoring tool for the management of intermediaries to prevent or detect any irregularities or fraudulent activities. We believe that these telephone recording requirements protect the interest of an intermediary and its clients, and you should take all necessary measures to ensure that they are being fully complied with. The SFC will take vigorous enforcement actions against any registered persons who  breach  these requirements with wilful intent.

Should you have any queries regarding the contents of this circular, please contact Ms Seine Luk on 2842 7696 .
